messages:
Ben: Getting paged? I wasn't. Noticed a spike in notify-service errors, a bunch of 401s to the pager webhook. No incident-bot pages so far.
Priya: I saw a couple of dropped pages earlier but assumed PD suppression. Can you paste the log snippet?
Ben: paste logs -> ```[2026-03-15T09:12:01Z] notify: webhook POST https://pager.example/v1/events -> 401 Unauthorized (x-request-id=abc123)
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] notify: enqueue failed, queue_size=4820
[2026-03-15T09:12:05Z] notify: webhook POST https://pager.example/v1/events -> 401 Unauthorized (x-request-id=abc124)```
Alex: 401s smell like either creds rotated or token header got dropped. Any deploys that touched secret-rotation or webhook proxy in last hour? @SRE-bot show recent deploys for service:notify
SRE-bot: deploybot: Recent deploys: notify-service v1.9.2 at 2026-03-15T08:45Z (by ci), secret-rotator v2.1.0 at 2026-03-15T08:50Z (by ops).
Maria: Secret-rotator did a scheduled KMS key rotation at 08:50 and pushed new webhook token to vault, but notify-service rollout only happened for a subset of replicas (staggered). Could be a mismatch window.
Priya: If rotator updated vault but notify pods still using old token and webhook proxy expects new token, we'd get 401s. Why didn't incident-bot page though? It reads notify events and should have created PD incidents for 5xx/4xx threshold.
Ben: incident-bot is running in a separate cluster and reads the notify queue via the notify webhook bridge. The bridge uses the same rotated token. If it's failing auth, bot won't receive events.
ops-oncall: I'm on pager duty rotator duty for the day, I didn't get any page. Can someone confirm whether notify->bridge webhook attempted retries or was suppressed?
Ben: Looks like the bridge returned 401s and the notify service started batching/enqueueing events. There's a suppression mechanism that avoids duplicate pages if queue > 1000 to prevent storming PD. That threshold kicked in.
Priya: Ok that explains no pages. We still need to get on-call alerted. Manual escalation now — who's on primary? @ops-oncall
ops-oncall: I'm primary. I can trigger manual PD incident if you give me the list of affected customers / alerts.
Alex: Quick mitigation path: 1) Roll secret-rotator back to previous token mapping OR 2) manually patch notify pods with the new token so they match the vault. Which is faster?
Maria: Patching pods will be faster. Backing out rotator risks leaving other consumers mismatched. I'll roll a one-off patch to set environment WEBHOOK_TOKEN on notify deployment to the vault value.
Ben: While Maria patches, create a temporary Slack-based pager bridge so we don't rely on the webhook flow. Steps: post an incident summary to #incidents-manual-paging and @ops-oncall will manually trigger PD.
Priya: Making manual channel now and inviting on-call + SRE. Creating channel #tmp-manual-pager-1976543210 :robot_face:
SRE-bot: incident-bot: created incident INC-20260315-42 (status: acknowledged) — note: auto-created = false (manual escalate)
Maria: Patching notify deployment with `kubectl set env deploy/notify WEBHOOK_TOKEN=redacted --namespace infra` (applied to the remaining replicas).
Ben: After patch: logs showing success -> ```[2026-03-15T09:16:44Z] notify: webhook POST https://pager.example/v1/events -> 202 Accepted (x-request-id=abc200)
[2026-03-15T09:16:45Z] notify: drain: sent=1200 queued=3600```
Priya: Good, bridge is receiving again? Can SRE-bot confirm it processed backlog? @SRE-bot process-status bridge:notify
SRE-bot: bridge-notify: processed backlog 1200 events in 30s, current queue=3600, health=degraded, retry-rate=2.8/s
ops-oncall: I'll manually open a PD incident and tag the top 10 affected customers. Doing it now.
ops-oncall: PD incident created: PD-83721, I put high priority and linked the Slack channel.
Alex: Follow-up tasks: 1) Add a temporary alert in console for webhook 401 > 5/min to page regardless of queue suppression. 2) Revisit the suppression threshold logic (current behavior prevents paging during mass-auth-failures). 3) Add canary rotation rollout steps: confirm bridge and notify handshake before rotating.
Maria: Filed runbook update PR: link=https://git.internal/r/redwood/runbooks/pull/128 (includes curl checks and `kubectl exec` commands to validate tokens).
Ben: Root cause: out-of-phase secret rotation where rotator updated vault and proxy expected new token but notify pods still used old token; suppression logic prevented automatic pages.
Priya: Postmortem action owner assignments: Maria -> rollout gating for secret-rotator, Alex -> alerting threshold changes, Ben -> add end-to-end test for notify->bridge auth during rotation. ops-oncall -> PD runbook addendum.
Maria: One more note: the rotator did not tag the change in vault with a rotation-id header; adding that would allow services to validate and log mismatches more clearly. I'll add it to the PR.
Priya: Thanks all. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours. If queue doesn't drop below 500 within 30m we'll schedule a controlled fallback to the alternate pager endpoint. :eyes:
